resources.string: A layout is a key grid. It types the language of the layout it is based on. A Bengali grid that you rearrange still uses the Bengali word list.
No layouts of your own yet
Copy a layout below to start from a grid that already works
Every layout that is on, and every one of your own, in one file. Import a layout reads it back
They are added to your layouts. A layout you already have stays as it is, and the copy comes in beside it.
Opens a .wmlayout.json file that someone shared
The app adds the layout to your layouts. Import and turn on makes it a keyboard you can switch to at once. Import alone leaves it off, and the switch on its row turns it on later.
The app imported %1$s and turned it on. Swipe the spacebar or hold the globe key to switch to it.
The app discards your changes to this built-in layout. The original grid comes back. Nothing else changes.
The app deletes this layout. If the layout is on under Languages, the app turns it off and the keyboard goes back to QWERTY.
The app could not write that file.
That file is not a WM Keyboard layout.
Read a layout file from FlorisBoard, HeliBoard, FUTO, Samsung Keyboard (Keys Cafe), Multiling O, Unexpected Keyboard, or a Windows, Mac or Linux computer

The app cannot read that file as a layout. FlorisBoard and HeliBoard layouts are .json or .txt files, FUTO layouts are .yaml files, Samsung Keyboard layouts shared from Keys Cafe are .kcf files, Multiling O layouts are text files with an OK_Layout_Begin block, a DIY layout or a settings export, and Unexpected Keyboard layouts are .xml files. Computer layouts are .klc files from Windows, .keylayout files from a Mac, and XKB symbols files from Linux. To import a FlorisBoard theme (.flex), go to Themes.
The app read this file as a FlorisBoard or HeliBoard layout. The other keyboard draws its own bottom row, so the app adds the delete, space and enter keys.
The app read this file as a HeliBoard text layout. That format holds letters only, so the app adds the delete, space and enter keys.
The app read this file as a FUTO Keyboard layout. The other keyboard draws the number row, the symbols and the alternate pages itself, so the app uses its own.
Read as a Keyman touch layout

The app read this file as a Samsung Keyboard layout made in Keys Cafe. The whole arrangement comes across as it was laid out, the bottom row included. Its row of numbers becomes this layout\'s number row.
The app read this as a Multiling O Keyboard layout. Its symbol pages and its AltGr page come across with it, and a key that types one thing on a tap and others on a swipe keeps its swipes.

The app read this file as a Windows layout made in MSKLC. The letter keys keep their places. The characters that AltGr and the dead keys type are on press and hold of the letters, and the symbol keys stay the ones you have.

The app read this file as a Mac layout (.keylayout). The letter keys keep their places. The characters that Option and the dead keys type are on press and hold of the letters, and the symbol keys stay the ones you have.

The app read this file as a Linux XKB layout. The letter keys keep their places. The characters that AltGr and the dead keys type are on press and hold of the letters, and the symbol keys stay the ones you have.

The app read this as an Unexpected Keyboard or CleverKeys layout. The swipes to the corners of each key come across as swipes, and you can also hold the key to get them. The app adds its own bottom row unless the layout has its own.
Read a .cin table, a Rime schema with its dictionaries, or an m17n .mim file. Pick all the files the method needs at the same time.
Reading the input method. A large Rime dictionary can take a minute.
The files are too large to import.
The app could not save the input method. Make sure there is free space on the device.
This layout does not exist any more.
This layout has no Fn layer yet. Add one, then put an Fn key on another layer to reach it.
Starts from Esc, F1 to F12, Tab, the arrows and Home/End
This is the built-in grid for the %1$s layer. If you change anything here, this layout gets its own copy of it.
This row is %1$.2f wide. The grid is %2$.2f.
Fit the row to the grid (%1$.2f)
Adds an empty row at the end of this layer
The keyboard shows this row above this layer. Tap a key to change it. Hold a key and drag it to move it.
Row in place of the digits
The number row already shows the digits, so the keyboard shows this row in place of the first row of this layer.
Add a key to this row
Draws each key as it looks when you hold shift
Reach anything that this screen has no control for
Puts the %1$s grid on the clipboard
The %1$s grid is on the clipboard. Paste it into another layer, into another layout, or into a message to share it.
Your device did not let the app write to the clipboard.
Replaces the %1$s grid with the layer on the clipboard
The %2$s layer now holds the %1$s grid from the clipboard.
The %1$s layer now holds the grid from the clipboard.
The clipboard does not hold a copied layer. Open the layer you want, then press Copy this layer.
The copied layer has no keys that this app can use.
Deletes your %1$s grid and uses the built-in one
You must fix this before you turn this layout on
Look at this, but the layout still works

Press a key to change it. Press and hold a key, then drag, to move it somewhere else in the grid, including into another row. Let go on the line between two rows, or above or below them all, to give the key a row of its own.
Your changes here do not affect typing until you turn the layout on under Languages.
This layout is on, so your changes affect typing straight away. The keyboard adds a delete, space or enter key back if you remove the last one.
Fix these problems in the layout editor first:
What the app draws on the key
Blank: the key types the label
Give the key a label or an output. A key with neither types nothing. The app deletes it when you turn the layout on.
The letters below set this. It is always the first of them.
Blank: one letter, as usual. Give more than one, such as qw, and the app finds the word you meant from all the keys you pressed.
This key stands for %1$s. It types %2$s while you type, and the app picks the word when you press space.
The press and hold popup does not hold these letters yet. It is the only way to spell a word that the app does not know.
Put the letters in the popup
Blank: shift types the capital letter of the label
The intent action that an automation app listens for, for example com.example.MACRO. If you leave it blank, the key does nothing.
1 to 6: dots 1-2-3 down the left column, 4-5-6 down the right
The secondary layout this key opens
No secondary layouts yet. Make one on the Key layouts screen first.
The keyboard mode this key turns on and off
No keyboard modes yet. Make one under Modes first.
More than one makes the key taller. The rows under it draw their keys around it.
Pick an icon to draw in place of the label
Draws the icon before the language name instead of in its place
There is no icon with the name \"%1$s\". The app draws the label instead
A short swipe from the key in any of eight directions types something else, so one key can carry nine characters
No centre character. A tap on this key types nothing; only its swipes do.
Tap a cell of the pad to set what a swipe that way types. A tap on the key still types the output. The keyboard draws the arms small on the key, and a swipe out to an arm and back types its capital.
Blank: no flick in this direction
A short swipe from the key in any of eight directions types something or does an action, such as moving the cursor
With an arm here, a swipe off this key is the arm, not a drag onto a letter for its combination. Clear the arms to have the drag back.
With an arm here, a swipe off this key is the arm, not the drag that peeks at the other layer. Holding it still, for a chord or the number pad, works either way. Clear the arms to have the peek back.
Tap a cell of the pad to set what a swipe that way types, or tap its bolt for an action. A tap on the key still does what the key does.
No flick this way. Tap to choose an action.
A flick this way does this: %1$s
Blank: shift types the capital letter of the flick
Becomes 小゛゜ after a kana
While the kana you are typing has a small, ゛ or ゜ form, this key changes it

The key shows 小゛゜ as soon as the last kana you typed can take a mark, and a tap changes that kana: か to が, は to ば and ぱ, つ to っ. When the word is done, or the last kana has no other form, the key goes back to its own action. Use it to put the 小゛゜ key on the globe or emoji key, and remove the separate 小゛゜ key to make room.
Holding the key keeps doing what it does, the way delete does

Hold the key and, after the same wait delete takes, it does its action over and over until you lift your finger. Arrow keys are what this is for: one press moves the cursor one place, and a hold walks it along. The two speeds are yours to set under Key press: Time before a key repeats, and Repeating key interval.
A press and hold on this key now repeats it, so its alternates cannot open any more. Turn the repeat off to get them back.

Holding a Select key turns selection mode on for as long as you hold it. If you give this key alternates, the long press opens them instead and hold to select stops working on it. Tap, double tap and triple tap still work either way.
Separate the entries with spaces, so an alternate cannot be a space. Entries of more than one character, such as .com, are correct. The app also draws the first one in the corner of the key.
How many alternates this key puts on a row

This is the column count for this key alone. Keys differ: a key with a dozen alternates reads better as a grid, and a key with three or four reads better as a single row.\n\nFrom settings leaves the key to the \"Alternate key columns\" setting under Key press, which is Automatic unless you changed it. A number from 3 to 11 gives this key that many columns whatever the setting says.
Extra entries in the same popup that do something instead of typing: Tab, voice typing, the editing pad. Tap one to change it.
Their place among the alternates in the popup

The actions usually go after all the alternates. Put them after a character and they are a short slide from the key, while a plain press and hold still types the first alternate. Put them first and a plain press and hold runs the first action. The actions stay together, in their own order. This needs Choose without lifting, under Key press, Alternate keys.
Runs as soon as you hold the key, with no popup. A delete or a cursor move repeats while you hold.
A press and hold on this key now runs its action, so its alternates cannot open any more. Remove the action to get them back.
The small mark in the corner of this key. Press and hold still opens the alternates
Settings has one switch for the hints on every key. Use this row when you want a different answer for this key: always draw it, or never draw it.
This key follows the one switch in Settings
This key always draws its corner hint
This key never draws its corner hint
Email and web address fields change the comma and full stop keys
Work it out from the key: a full stop or a comma on the bottom row fills its slot
An email field puts @ here. A web field keeps the comma and puts / first on its press and hold
An email field and a web field add .com and the other endings to the long press
No slot and no substitution: the key types what you put on it, so a full stop stays a full stop on a language that ends sentences some other way
The label, or the output if you set one
Press for one capital letter. Press two times for caps lock
Follow the theme and the settings
Only this layout changes. The others keep the size from Layout and size, or from your theme.
Makes every label on this layout larger or smaller than the size in Settings. It does not change the size on other layouts.
Label size on this layer: follows the layout
Sets the size for the %1$s grid only. Every other layer keeps the layout size below.
Automatic draws one letter large and a word small. Set a size to choose for this key.
Hint size: same as every key
The corner hint on this key alone, larger or smaller than on the others
A key for one way up takes no room the other way, and the rest of its row closes up
Draw another layout\'s keys while the phone is turned sideways. It has to type the same way as this one
On a tablet, add tab, backslash, caps lock, a second shift and the arrow keys around this layout
This layout is not one the tablet keys can be added to, so this setting has no effect on it
Turns caps lock on and off with one press. For wide layouts that also have a shift key
Backspace. It repeats while you hold it
⌦ deletes the text after the cursor. It repeats while you hold it
A swipe on this key moves the cursor or changes the layout
Does the app\'s own action: send, search or done
Always types a line break, even where enter would send
Changes the last kana you typed to its small, ゛ or ゜ form: か to が, は to ば to ぱ, つ to っ
Adds a stroke to the last Korean letter you typed: ㄱ to ㅋ, ㄴ to ㄷ to ㅌ, ㅏ to ㅑ, and back
Changes the last Korean consonant you typed to its double form and back: ㄱ to ㄲ, ㅂ to ㅃ
A scrolling list in place of the key. While you type on a T9 pinyin pad it lists the syllables your keys could spell, to pick one; otherwise it lists the key\'s long-press characters
Switches Chinese candidates between Simplified (简体) and Traditional (繁體) characters. The same setting as Traditional characters on the Chinese screen
Goes back to the letter grid
Opens the grid of every tool, like the button at the start of the toolbar
Changes to the next layout that you turned on
Opens the system list of the keyboards on your device, so you can change to a different one
Changes to the Fn grid of this layout for one key
Applies to the next key. Press two times to lock it
Sends a real Tab key press
Sends a real Esc key press
Moves the cursor up a line
Moves the cursor down a line
One dot of a braille chord of six keys. Set the dot number below
Adds a short signal. The letter commits after a pause
Adds a long signal. The letter commits after a pause
Goes straight to one other keyboard app on your device, with no list. Pick the keyboard below
The keyboard app this key switches to
No other keyboards are turned on. Enable one in your device\'s keyboard settings first.
Shows one of your secondary layouts over the letters. Press the key again, or an ABC key, to go back. Pick the layout below
Turns one of your keyboard modes on, the way picking it from the Modes tool does. Press it again to go back to automatic. Pick the mode below
Opens one of the keyboard tools, such as voice typing or the editing pad. Pick the tool below
Sends an Android broadcast for automation apps such as Tasker. Set the action below
A gap on purpose. The app draws empty space and ignores presses

This is the layout as the app stores it. Edit here to reach anything that the grid editor has no control for. When you open this screen again, the app formats the text again. It leaves out the values that match the default, and it does not keep your spacing.
That is not valid layout JSON.

A secondary layout is not a language. It shows over the letters of the layout you type with, and it keeps that layout\'s dictionary. Open it with a key set to the Open a layout action, or with the Secondary layout tool.
This layout is live as soon as a key or the Secondary layout tool opens it. It does not appear under Languages.
For this layer only, over the keyboard-wide Show flick arms on keys setting

Flick keys draw the characters they type in each direction on the key face. Turn this off for a pad whose flicks you already know, and keep them on another, such as the number pad. While it matches the keyboard-wide setting, this layer follows that setting.
The layer stays on screen when the keyboard closes or the field changes. Make sure you have a way to exit this layout.
The panel stays open when the keyboard closes or the field changes. Make sure you have a way to exit this panel.

Normally a panel closes each time the keyboard opens on a new field. With this on, the panel stays until you press a key or a tool that goes somewhere else, or the Back button. The keyboard cannot close it by itself.

Normally the keyboard goes back to the letters each time it opens. With this on, the layer stays until you press a key or a tool that goes somewhere else. The keyboard cannot take you off it by itself, so the layer needs an ABC key, a symbols key, or the Secondary layout tool on the toolbar.
The keyboard shows the bottom row of this layer differently, because of these Bottom row keys settings. The grid above shows the row as the keyboard does:
Keep this bottom row as it is here
Moving or changing a key that the settings changed turns this on
The Bottom row keys settings do not change this layer

The Bottom row keys settings change the bottom row of every layout. They can hide the 🌐 key, move it, swap it with the comma, or make it an emoji key. With this on, this layer keeps its bottom row as you make it here, and those settings do not change it. When you turn this on, or move or change a key that the settings changed, the layer keeps the row as the keyboard showed it, so no key moves. Turn this off to let the settings change the row again. On a layer you have not changed in any other way, turning it off also puts back the standard row.
Change what the keyboard does to the bottom row of every layout
Inherit the theme that is set
Inherit the theme of the layout
Inherit the theme of the layout

While this layout is on screen, the keyboard uses this theme. It replaces the theme you set elsewhere, and an automatic light and dark pair, for as long as the layout shows. A layer with a theme of its own uses that one instead. Your own choice does not change.

Most layouts should leave this alone: the language you chose above already knows the right method. Set it when this layout types the same language a different way, such as a phonetic grid and a direct grid for one script.
The language above decides the method
A key types its own character. Nothing joins
Press an accent key, then a letter, and the two join
Type roman letters and the keyboard writes the script
A consonant and a vowel sign join into one cluster
Jamo join into a syllable block while you type
Type aa for â, and as for á
Type a6 for â, and a1 for á
Type the sound in roman letters, then select the character
Type the strokes of the character in order
Pinyin on nine keys, with several letters on each key
Type the bopomofo symbols, then select the character
Type the shape codes of the character
The first Cangjie code and the last one only
Type Cantonese sounds in roman letters
Type Bangla phonetically by Borno's keymap, where c is চ and ch is ছ
Type Bangla in lowercase letters, with f and / as modifiers
Khipro, but letters only join when you press / after them
Make Korean vowels from the strokes ㅣ ㆍ ㅡ, and tap a consonant key again for its next letter
Korean, with ㅐ and ㅔ typed as ㅏ or ㅓ and then ㅣ
Draw the grid at the height you actually type at

The preview normally keeps the keys within a comfortable range so the whole grid fits on this screen. Turn this on to see your real proportions, which matters if you type at a tall key height. The preview stays at the top either way. A grid that is then taller than the space it has scrolls inside that space.
The panels every layout uses unless it has a panel grid of its own. Each layout\'s editor has a tab for every panel.
This layout uses the shared %1$s panel. Changing anything here makes a copy for this layout only. The shared panel is under Key layouts, Panel layouts.
Drops this layout\'s own %1$s grid. The shared panel comes back.
Arrange the keys and the parts of this panel
Press a cell to change it. Component cells hold the live parts of the panel. Rows with a component share the height that the key rows leave.
Turn on the GIF or Sticker tool
The switch stays empty on the keyboard until one of the two tools is on: with only emoji in it, there is nowhere to switch to.
The keyboard uses your changes at once.
Go back to the panel the app ships with
The panel goes back to the layout the app ships with. Your arrangement is deleted.
A live part of the panel: the emoji grid, the clipboard history, a search box
Which part of the panel this cell shows
Runs them in turn, such as start of line then page up
Tap one above to take it out
Arrows, word moves, page up and down, start and end of the line and of the text, Select, Select all, Cut, Copy, Paste and Delete. Pick the operation below
What this key does to the text
No space after the next key

In an email address field the keyboard changes two keys on this layer. The comma key types @, and the press and hold of the full stop starts with .com and the other endings. To keep a key as you made it, open the key and set Field adaptation, under More, to Exactly as laid out.

In a web address field, such as the address bar of a browser, the keyboard changes keys on this layer. The comma key keeps its comma but its press and hold, and its corner hint, start with /. The full stop gets .com and the other endings, and enter shows Go. To keep a key as you made it, open the key and set Field adaptation, under More, to Exactly as laid out.
The keyboard shows this row under this layer when Arrow keys row is on in Layout and size. You can add any key to it, such as Word left or a second Shift.
Row in place of the digits, key %1$d
What the corner of the key shows. It does not change what a press and hold types. Blank shows the first alternate.
What the corner of the key shows, for example ,?! on a full stop. It does not change what a press and hold types. Blank shows %1$s.
How the keyboard shows it. The outlined entry is what a plain press and hold types.
How the keyboard shows it. The outlined entry is what a plain press and hold types. Faded entries come from your settings, such as the press and hold shortcuts and the accents, not from this layout.
Press keys to pick them, and press one again to put it back. Keys side by side in one row move together, with the arrows or by dragging one of them.
To move them together, pick keys that sit side by side in one row.

plurals.item: Copied %d key, with its flicks, icon, corner hint and alternates. Pick a key in any layer or layout and press Paste after.
Copied %d keys, with their flicks, icons, corner hints and alternates. Pick a key in any layer or layout and press Paste after.

resources.string: The clipboard holds no keys. Copy a key in the layout editor first.
A key that runs this text-editing operation.
Every key keeps its share. A row narrower than the grid (%1$.2f) is drawn centred, like the second row of QWERTY.
